name: core.openwop.workflows.career-search
description: Career search + apply (ADR 0543 P2/P3). `career.search` scores and screens a posting; `career.apply` checks a proposed résumé rewrite for fabrication and then STARTS a browser session carrying the apply-grant context. Neither chain submits: the ADR 0541 commit gate owns that decision, so an edited chain cannot route around the grant.
author: OpenWOP App

chains.label: Career: score & screen a role
chains.description: Scores a job posting against your profile and checks it against any bar the posting STATES. Ends with a verdict you can act on — it never applies to anything, because submitting is bounded by an apply grant you issue separately. Parameters are OPTIONAL with `{}` defaults (ADR 0504): a required whole-value `{{params.X}}` would freeze to undefined when instantiated without params and fail mid-run naming an internal node instead of the parameter.

digest.description: The job posting: title, companyName, skills[], location, remote, sponsorship and any stated citizenship/clearance requirement.

profile.description: What you are looking for: skills[], targetTitles[], salaryFloor, wantsRemote.

applicant.description: What you can clear: requiresSponsorship, meetsCitizenshipRequirement, holdsRequiredClearance. Absent means 'needs nothing', so only a bar the posting STATES can disqualify.

eligible.description: Whether a JD-STATED bar disqualifies this role for this applicant. True unless a stated bar fires.

reason.description: Why it was disqualified, or empty when eligible.

quote.description: The posting's OWN words backing a disqualification — what makes a skip checkable rather than something to trust.

matchScore.description: Weighted fit score against the applicant's profile, recorded at decision time.

chains.label: Career: prepare & start an application
chains.description: Checks a proposed résumé rewrite against its source for fabricated numbers, employers and dates, then starts a browser session to fill the application. It does NOT submit — the commit gate consults your apply grant and, without one, stops and asks you first.

original.description: The résumé bullet as written on your CV.

reworded.description: The tailored rewrite to check before it is used.

allowedEmployers.description: Employers you genuinely have, umbrella names included.

orgId.description: The organization this application belongs to.

allowedOrigins.description: Origins the session may reach — the grant is scoped to these too.

applyContext.description: subjectId + campaignId + tier. Without it the commit gate has nothing to consult and every submission asks you first.

inputs.task: Fill in this job application using the applicant's profile. Do not submit; the host decides that.

sessionId.description: The browser session. Its status is `awaiting_approval` whenever no grant covers the submission.

guardOk.description: False when the rewrite introduced a fact the source does not support — the session is not started.

violations.description: What the guard rejected, each naming the offending token.

chains.label: Career: run a campaign pass
chains.description: Runs one pass of your standing job-search campaign: every stored listing is screened, scored and — where a board ships a submit lane and your apply grant allows it — applied to, under the grant's ceiling, hourly pace and your daily cap. Takes no parameters by design: targeting comes from your steering policy, authority from grants you issued, answers from your answer bank. The output is the pass digest — what was applied, parked, and skipped, each with its reason. Registered under its stable id so the career agent's board cards can name it (WF-JS-1 / ADR 0543 D3).

ranGrants.description: Active grants the pass ran under.

skippedNoSubmitLane.description: Listings whose board ships no submit lane yet — the coverage gap as a number.

skippedDailyCap.description: Items not attempted because the day's cap was already spent.

results.description: Per-grant digest: applied dealIds, parked count, and every skip with its reason.
